newsitem.title: THAILAND: Toyota to sell Asian cars in Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to sell Asian cars in Thailand.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corporation will launch its first sale of 40,000 units of its new "Soluna" Asian cars in Thailand in 1997, its vice chairman Iwao Isomura said on Monday.
Toyota said the new cars would be sold in Thailand from January 31, 1997. Production of the cars at its Thai factory at Cherchengsao near Bangkok began last month.
Toyota said the Soluna was its most important current strategic project.

"The AFC (affordable family car) is the most important project of Toyota. For a world strategy this is the car for which we expect the market to grow most rapidly and it will affect many countries in the region into the next century," said Yoshiaki Muramatsu, president of Toyota Motor Thailand.

To keep costs to a minimum, around 700 of the Soluna's components, or 70 percent, have been sourced either from Thailand or the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries, said Soluna chief engineer Takeshi Yoshida.
ASEAN groups Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Vietnam, Brunei and the Philippines.
Components are interchangeable between the two models while assembly time at Toyota's seven billion baht Thai factory has been minimized but quality standards maintained, he said.
Toyota is the dominant car supplier in Thailand.
